h1: The 6 Best Under-Desk Filing Cabinets of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Under-Desk File Cabinets: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six under-desk filing cabinets compared on drawers, locks, rolling bases, materials and fit for small home offices.
summary: The Letaya 3-drawer is the best under-desk filing cabinet: lockable, metal, fully assembled and legal-friendly. The SISESOL is the cheapest lockable steel option and the narrowest fit. The SteeLoong is a plain pedestal, the GYIIYUO adds a 24 inch top for L-shaped desks, and the DEVAISE doubles as a printer stand. The BYNSOE is for roomy desks only.
intro: Buyers measure desk width and forget the three numbers that decide whether an under-desk cabinet works: clearance below the modesty panel, drawer travel and knee space. A pedestal that technically fits can still bark your shins or refuse to open all the way. That is how a cheap cabinet becomes a doorstop in a hallway, and a refund headache you could have avoided with one tape measure.

We reviewed eight listings and kept six that clearly suit under-desk use, setting aside a lateral cabinet that needs more width. Ranking weighs drawer count, locks, material, mobility, assembly state and price bucket, drawn from spec sheets and owner feedback. Nothing here was bench measured, so confirm your own clearance, depth and paper size before ordering anything at all.

products.name: Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet with Lock, Under Desk Metal Filing Cabinet, Fully Assembled
products.verdict: A lockable metal pedestal that arrives built.
products.description:
The Letaya is a three-drawer metal pedestal with a lock, delivered fully assembled and sized for under-desk use. It takes letter, legal and A4 paper, so a mixed archive of contracts and tax records goes in one place. Metal matters here: full hanging folders are heavy, and steel runners hold their line where fabric or thin plastic sags.

It ranks first because the third drawer adds capacity without widening the footprint, and skipping assembly removes the worst part of the job. Against two-drawer rivals in the same $50 to $100 bucket, such as the SteeLoong, you simply get more storage for the same money.

Buy it if you keep a real paper archive. The caveat is height. Three drawers stand taller than a two-drawer unit, so measure the floor-to-desk gap before ordering.
products.idealFor: Home offices with a real paper archive.
products.skipIf: Your desk has very low clearance.

products.name: SISESOL 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Narrow Vertical Filing Cabinet, Under Desk File Cabinet
products.verdict: The cheapest lockable metal cabinet with a narrow fit.
products.description:
The SISESOL is a narrow, vertical, two-drawer steel cabinet with a lock. It accepts letter, A4 and legal files, which is wider paper support than its price suggests. The slim profile slides into tight kneeholes where a standard pedestal would stick out, and assembly is simple.

It takes second place because it costs the least of the metal group, in the $25 to $50 bucket, while keeping both the lock and legal capability. It trails the Letaya by one drawer and has no casters listed, so there is no rolling it out to reach files at the back.

Buy it for a small desk, a dorm or a tight budget. The caveat is that it stays put: once you load it with folders, moving it means lifting, and two drawers cap how much paper it holds.
products.skipIf: You want to roll it out to reach files.

products.name: SteeLoong 2 Drawer File Cabinets, Metal Office File Cabinet with Lock, Black
products.verdict: No extras, just a compact black metal pedestal.
products.description:
The SteeLoong is the cabinet you buy when you want nothing extra. It offers two lockable drawers, a compact metal pedestal footprint and a black finish that disappears into most offices. It handles standard file sizes without drama.

It ranks third because the SISESOL gives you the same two locking steel drawers for a lower price, in the $25 to $50 bucket against the SteeLoong's $50 to $100. Nothing in the listing shows a clearly narrower body to justify the gap. What you get instead is a tidy, uniform look.

Buy it if appearance matters in a shared or client-facing office. The caveat is that the listing is thin: no wheels, no work surface and no stated legal-size support, so confirm your paper size before ordering.
products.skipIf: You want wheels or a work surface.

products.name: GYIIYUO 2 Drawer File Cabinet with 24 Inch Extended Desktop, Mobile Filing Cabinet with Side Bag
products.verdict: A rolling cabinet that adds a 24 inch extended top.
products.description:
The GYIIYUO takes a different path. It pairs two fabric-fronted drawers with a 24 inch extended top, rolling casters and a side storage bag, so it works as a movable return beside an L-shaped desk. Casters let you roll it out to reach files, then park it back under the edge.

It ranks fourth because fabric is lighter than steel, no lock is listed, and fabric drawers sag under full hanging folders. The trade is mobility and surface area: neither the Letaya nor the SISESOL gives you extra desk space.

Buy it if you want a rolling cabinet that doubles as a work surface. The caveat is security and strength. Without a lock it is poor for financial records, and heavy files will droop the fabric over time, so keep loads light.

products.name: DEVAISE Mobile File Cabinet, Rolling Printer Stand with Open Storage Shelf, Fabric Vertical Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: Filing drawer and printer perch in one rolling unit.
products.description:
The DEVAISE combines a rolling fabric file drawer with an open top shelf sized for a printer. It takes A4 or letter paper and rolls on casters. In a small room, the shelf solves two problems at once: where to put the printer and where to file what it prints.

It ranks fifth because it gives up locking security for versatility. The steel pedestals above protect records, while this one protects floor space. The fabric drawer is lightweight, and nothing in the listing mentions a lock.

Buy it if a printer needs a home and your paperwork is not sensitive. The caveat is load. A heavy laser printer on top makes the unit harder to roll, and a printer's weight sitting above a fabric drawer is not an ideal arrangement for dense folders.
products.idealFor: Small rooms needing a printer spot.

products.name: BYNSOE 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Vertical Filing Storage Cabinet, Steel, Assembly Required
products.verdict: A standard steel cabinet that you must measure for.
products.description:
The BYNSOE is a vertical steel cabinet with two lockable drawers and a standard file-cabinet footprint. It requires assembly, accepts letter-size paper only and carries no legal or A4 support in the listing. The steel body is its strength: it will hold a full set of hanging folders without bowing.

It ranks last because the standard footprint is wider than the narrow under-desk profile of the SISESOL, and the paper support is narrower than the Letaya's for the same $50 to $100 bucket. It is a general cabinet, not a purpose-built pedestal.

Buy it if you have a roomy desk and want plain steel. The caveat is fit. Measure clearance, width and depth carefully before ordering, because this is the pick most likely to refuse to slide under a standard desk.
products.skipIf: You need a narrow under-desk fit.

whatMatters.detail: Clearance is the gap between the floor and the underside of your desk, plus depth to the modesty panel. A pedestal even a few inches too tall will not slide in, and one too deep will jam against the wall. Measure both with a tape, then compare against the listing dimensions before you weigh locks and casters.

Drawer count sets capacity and height. Two drawers suit most home offices and fit under standard desks, while three, like the Letaya, suit a real archive and need extra clearance. Count the folders you keep today, then choose the smallest option that holds them with a little room to spare for growth.

A lock keeps financial and personal records away from visitors, roommates and kids. It matters most in shared rooms or dorms. Check the listing title for the word lock, as the Letaya and SISESOL show, and confirm that keys are included. A lock is privacy, not real security against a determined thief or a pry bar.

Steel carries the weight of full hanging folders without bowing, while fabric drawers like those on the GYIIYUO and DEVAISE sag over time under dense paper. Fabric is lighter and cheaper to move. Read the material line in the specs, and pick fabric only for light loads that you do not need to protect or lock.

Letter paper is the US default, while legal sheets run longer and A4 is slightly narrower and longer than letter. A drawer that fits only letter, like the BYNSOE, will crush or reject anything else. Look for legal or A4 in the listing bullets if your files include contracts or imported paperwork from abroad.

faq.q: Will a cabinet fit under every desk?
faq.a: No. Measure clearance height and depth first, then compare them with the listing dimensions. The three-drawer Letaya is taller than two-drawer models like the SISESOL, so a low desk can rule it out completely.

faq.q: Can I store legal size files?
faq.a: Only if the listing says so. The Letaya and SISESOL list legal support, while the BYNSOE lists letter only. Confirm the paper size before you buy, since a drawer that is too narrow will crush legal sheets.

faq.q: Is a fabric cabinet good enough?
faq.a: For light paper, yes. The GYIIYUO and DEVAISE hold occasional files fine. For dense hanging folders, a steel pedestal like the Letaya or SteeLoong stays stable, while fabric tends to sag over time and loses shape.
The Letaya arrives fully assembled, which is a real advantage. The BYNSOE and the SISESOL need assembly, so plan some time for it, keep a screwdriver handy and check that all hardware is in the box.

faq.q: Do the locks keep thieves out?
faq.a: They are meant for casual privacy, not security. A lock on the Letaya or SISESOL stops curious roommates, not a determined thief. Keep sensitive originals like passports, deeds and tax records in a proper fireproof safe.

faq.q: Can I move a rolling cabinet with a full load?
faq.a: Casters help, but a full cabinet is heavy. On the GYIIYUO or DEVAISE, lock the wheels when parked, avoid overloading, and remember that a printer on top shifts the center of gravity, making tipping more likely.

finalTake: Most home offices should buy the Letaya: three lockable metal drawers, legal support and no assembly. The SISESOL is the budget answer for tight desks. Choose the GYIIYUO for an L-shaped desk or the DEVAISE if a printer needs a spot, and accept the weaker fabric and missing locks. Measure your clearance first, because fit decides everything.
